paragraphs: A model can support efficient basic calculations while still making a more complicated inference question difficult. This paper studies that gap for models represented as computational circuits. Its central idea is to express complex questions as combinations of simpler circuit operations, so that their computational feasibility can be understood piece by piece.

The authors analyze sums, products, quotients, powers, logarithms, and exponentials. For each kind of transformation, they identify structural conditions on the circuits that are sufficient for efficient computation. They also establish new hardness results for cases where relevant properties are absent. These results distinguish supported routes to efficient inference from settings where computation becomes provably difficult.

Combining these operations yields a common framework for questions ranging from expectations of decision-tree ensembles to information-theoretic divergences between sum-product networks. The contribution is therefore both organizational and constructive: it brings earlier tractability results together and derives additional tractable inference scenarios. The structural conditions provide sufficient guarantees, rather than a claim that every efficient calculation must satisfy them.
neurips-2021-a-compositional-atlas-of-tr.tldr: The paper builds a modular framework for determining when circuit operations can support efficient probabilistic inference.

paragraphs: Neurons can produce different numbers of spikes even under apparently identical conditions. This variability can contain information about neural computation, but studying it often requires repeated experimental trials or restrictive assumptions about its distribution. This paper develops a probabilistic model that can examine changing spike-count distributions without requiring repeatable trials.

The approach uses sparse Gaussian processes to connect observed variables and unobserved factors to arbitrary spike-count distributions. Scalable variational inference jointly learns these relationships and the trajectories of the hidden factors. It can also model joint distributions across neurons, allowing shared statistical dependencies to be associated with interpretable latent influences.

Applied to mouse head-direction cells, the model reveals variability that does not follow the simple relationship with average spike count assumed by standard models. External variables can modulate variability about as strongly as they modulate mean firing rate, while slow, low-dimensional hidden factors explain away correlations between neurons. These findings support studying variability as a structured signal in its own right, including under conditions beyond repeated sensory experiments.
neurips-2021-a-universal-probabilistic-s.tldr: A flexible spike-count model finds structured changes in neural variability without requiring repeated experimental trials.

paragraphs: Multi-head self-attention allows a neural network to relate information from several learned perspectives. Within each head, keys and queries provide the representations used to determine attention relationships. This paper proposes explicitly encouraging their distributions to match, introducing an additional learning objective called alignment attention.

The alignment objective works as unsupervised regularization within an existing attention framework. This makes it possible to adapt models that already use self-attention, including pretrained models. The approach changes how attention representations are encouraged to organize during optimization, while retaining the broader framework in which those representations are used.

Across language-understanding tasks, the authors report benefits in accuracy, uncertainty estimation, transfer across domains, and resistance to adversarial attacks. They also demonstrate applications to graph attention and visual question answering. These results suggest that distribution matching can be useful across multiple attention-based settings. Its significance extends beyond prediction accuracy: the reported improvements also concern how reliably a model expresses uncertainty and behaves when its inputs or evaluation domain change.
neurips-2021-alignment-attention-by-matc.tldr: Alignment attention regularizes each attention head by matching key and query distributions, improving several measures of model reliability in experiments.

paragraphs: Reinforcement learning can require enormous amounts of experience unless the problem has useful structure. This paper introduces Bellman Eluder dimension as a way to describe structure that supports learning with relatively few samples. The aim is to bring many previously tractable problem families under a shared complexity measure.

The authors show that problems with low Bellman Eluder dimension include tabular and linear Markov decision processes, reactive partially observable problems, and families characterized by low Bellman rank or low Eluder dimension. They introduce an optimization-based algorithm, GOLF, and provide a new analysis of the existing hypothesis-elimination algorithm OLIVE.

For low-dimension problems, both algorithms have guarantees for learning nearly optimal policies using a number of samples polynomial in the relevant parameters and independent of state-action-space size. For several established subclasses, the regret and sample-complexity guarantees match or improve earlier results. The significance is conditional on the structural measure being small: large state and action spaces can still permit sample-efficient learning when this form of complexity remains controlled.
neurips-2021-bellman-eluder-dimension-ne.tldr: Bellman Eluder dimension unifies many tractable reinforcement-learning settings and supports sample-efficiency guarantees for two algorithms.

paragraphs: Clustering usually seeks centers that keep an overall distance-based cost small. This paper also considers an individual fairness requirement: every point should have a center within a radius determined by its local neighborhood. Specifically, that radius is its distance to the n/k-th nearest point, where n is the number of points and k is the number of centers.

The authors use linear programming and modify existing rounding techniques to obtain clustering algorithms with better cost guarantees. Their approach covers objectives including k-median and k-means. It improves the worst-case objective guarantee over the earlier local-search approach while retaining comparable theoretical guarantees on approximate fairness.

In experiments, the resulting costs are extremely close to optimal, and solutions are noticeably fairer than those from the earlier approach. Solving the linear program exactly can be computationally prohibitive, so the authors also use sparsification to substantially improve runtime in practice. The contribution combines stronger theoretical cost control with empirical improvements in both cost and individual access to nearby centers.
neurips-2021-better-algorithms-for-indiv.tldr: Linear-programming-based clustering improves cost guarantees and empirically produces fairer solutions under neighborhood-based individual fairness constraints.

paragraphs: In online multiclass classification, a learner repeatedly predicts a label and receives feedback. This paper allows the available feedback to be specified by an arbitrary directed graph. That setting includes bandit feedback but can also describe richer information patterns relevant to filtering and label-efficient classification.

The proposed algorithm, Gappletron, handles arbitrary feedback graphs. For a broad class of surrogate losses, the authors prove regret bounds both in expectation and with high probability. The bounds scale as B times the square root of rho K T, where B measures prediction-space diameter, K counts classes, T counts rounds, and rho is the graph's domination number. This graph parameter captures an aspect of the exploration requirement.

With full information, the surrogate-regret bound becomes constant in the number of rounds, scaling as B squared times K. A general lower bound shows that the upper bounds have limited room for improvement. Synthetic experiments also find competitive performance across several feedback graphs, complementing the theoretical account of how feedback structure affects learning.
neurips-2021-beyond-bandit-feedback-in-o.tldr: Gappletron learns under arbitrary graph-defined feedback and comes with regret guarantees that reflect the available information.

paragraphs: Learning through categorical random choices requires estimating how model parameters affect an objective despite the choices being discrete. Such gradient estimates can be noisy. CARMS addresses this problem by coordinating multiple samples so that they are negatively correlated, making repeated selections less common and reducing estimation variance.

The method combines REINFORCE with copula-based sampling to construct these jointly antithetic samples. Because changing the sampling relationships could otherwise distort the estimate, importance sampling keeps the gradient estimator unbiased. This means its expected value remains the intended gradient while its sampling variability can be reduced.

CARMS also connects existing estimators within one framework. With two categories it recovers the binary ARMS estimator, and with independent samples it recovers the leave-one-out REINFORCE estimator known as LOORF or VarGrad. Experiments on generative modeling and structured-output prediction find that CARMS outperforms competing methods, including a strong self-control baseline. The results support coordinated sampling as a useful way to improve discrete-variable learning without introducing gradient-estimation bias.
neurips-2021-carms-categorical-antitheti.tldr: CARMS uses negatively correlated categorical samples to reduce gradient-estimation variance while preserving unbiasedness.

paragraphs: N:M sparsity imposes a local pattern on network weights: N of every M consecutive elements must be zero. Pruning and fine-tuning can preserve accuracy for many models under this constraint. This paper asks whether rearranging channels can make the required sparsity pattern less damaging, particularly for small networks with few spare parameters.

The method permutes weight matrices along their channel dimension and adjusts surrounding layers accordingly. These rearrangements change how weights are grouped for sparsity without adding inference runtime. The authors introduce a quality metric for comparing permutations and efficient search procedures, including two techniques intended to escape local minima.

Experiments show improved sparse-network accuracy, including accuracy recovery for small, parameter-efficient models, with insignificant additional training overhead. An ablation study examines the contributions of the search components, and further results show correlation between the proposed quality metric and final accuracy. The paper also demonstrates conversion of unstructured sparse workloads into structured ones. Together, these findings show that channel arrangement is a useful degree of freedom when imposing local sparsity constraints.
neurips-2021-channel-permutations-for-n-.tldr: Reordering network channels improves accuracy under N:M sparsity without changing inference runtime.

paragraphs: Controllable image generation requires a model to follow requested attributes, including combinations it has not previously encountered. This paper uses energy-based models to express those attribute preferences within the latent space of a pretrained generator. Working in that space makes the approach applicable to high-resolution image synthesis.

The proposed energy formulation describes data and attributes jointly, and sampling is expressed as solving an ordinary differential equation. Given a pretrained generator such as StyleGAN, the additional training requirement is an attribute classifier. The authors report efficient latent-space sampling that is robust to hyperparameter choices, alongside a simple and fast training procedure.

Experiments show better conditional sampling and sequential editing than the state-of-the-art methods evaluated. The approach also performs strongly when generating unseen attribute combinations without examples of those combinations. By combining energy functions through logical operators, the authors demonstrate compositional generation of photorealistic images at 1024 by 1024 resolution and claim the first such result. The contribution connects reusable attribute controls with an existing generator's image-production capabilities.
neurips-2021-controllable-and-compositio.tldr: Latent-space energy models enable efficient attribute-controlled generation and unseen attribute combinations with a pretrained image generator.

paragraphs: Vision-and-language navigation asks an agent to move through an indoor environment while following human instructions. Training examples differ in difficulty, but earlier approaches often overlook that distribution. The authors argue that ignoring these differences may weaken learning and propose organizing training through a curriculum.

Their training paradigm balances human prior knowledge about examples with the agent's learning progress. This combines an externally informed view of difficulty with information about how training is actually proceeding. The paper develops principles for curriculum design and rearranges the Room-to-Room benchmark dataset so it can support this form of training.

Experiments report significant improvements in navigation performance, generalization, and training efficiency for existing state-of-the-art agents. The approach is described as model-agnostic and achieves these gains without increasing model complexity. Its practical significance is that changes to the organization of training can improve how an existing agent learns. The reported benefits concern both successful navigation and the efficiency and transferability of the learning process, rather than requiring a larger navigation architecture.
neurips-2021-curriculum-learning-for-vis.tldr: A curriculum balancing human knowledge and agent progress improves navigation learning without increasing model complexity.

paragraphs: BinaryConnect is widely used as a foundation for neural-network quantization, yet its optimization behavior has been less well understood. This paper examines the mathematical relationships behind BinaryConnect and related methods. The authors show that algorithms often treated separately, including post-training quantization, have substantial similarities.

They argue that proximal maps provide a useful family of quantizers because they are comparatively straightforward to design and analyze. They also refine the connection between BinaryConnect and dual averaging, then place dual averaging within the broader generalized conditional-gradient framework. These links make established optimization ideas available for understanding quantized-network training.

Building on this analysis, the authors introduce ProxConnect as a generalization of BinaryConnect and prove convergence properties through the identified connections. Experiments on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet find competitive performance. The contribution therefore combines a clearer account of existing methods with a new algorithm supported by theory and empirical evaluation. The experimental claim is competitiveness, while the mathematical contribution concerns how quantization methods can be organized and analyzed within shared optimization frameworks.
neurips-2021-demystifying-and-generalizi.tldr: ProxConnect generalizes BinaryConnect through proximal quantizers and established optimization connections, with convergence results and competitive experiments.

paragraphs: An event sequence contains both occurrences and their timing, making unusual temporal patterns a distinct detection problem. This paper treats anomalous continuous-time sequences as observations outside the distribution described by a temporal point process. That framing connects anomaly detection to a probabilistic model of how events unfold over time.

The authors first examine goodness-of-fit tests, which assess whether observed data agree with a proposed model. They demonstrate limitations in popular statistics used for temporal point processes and introduce a new test designed to address those shortcomings. The method can work with different point-process models, including neural ones, and is described as easy to implement.

Experiments assess both conventional goodness-of-fit testing and anomaly detection on simulated and real-world data. The proposed statistic performs strongly in both roles. This matters because checking model agreement and identifying unusual sequences become parts of the same statistical approach. The contribution centers on the testing statistic and its compatibility with multiple models, making it applicable beyond one particular temporal point-process architecture.
neurips-2021-detecting-anomalous-event-s.tldr: A new goodness-of-fit statistic improves detection of anomalous event sequences across temporal point-process models.

paragraphs: This paper studies whether an unknown shallow ReLU network can be learned with provably efficient computation and data use. The network applies a linear transformation and biases, passes the results through ReLU activations, and combines them into an output. A central feature is that the hidden units can have nonzero biases.

Earlier learning results considered in the abstract assume those biases are zero. To handle their presence, the authors use a Hermite expansion of the network's function and robustly decompose several higher-order tensors arising from that expansion. These mathematical objects provide a route to recovering the network despite the additional complexity introduced by biases.

The resulting algorithms run in polynomial time and use polynomially many samples under Gaussian inputs and mild non-degeneracy assumptions. The authors also establish identifiability of network parameters under very mild assumptions, addressing whether parameters can be determined from the function they produce. The contribution expands the class of shallow ReLU networks covered by efficient-learning theory while retaining explicit conditions on the input distribution and network structure.
neurips-2021-efficient-algorithms-for-le.tldr: Tensor-based algorithms efficiently learn shallow ReLU networks with biases under Gaussian inputs and mild non-degeneracy assumptions.

paragraphs: Hierarchical Bayesian models share information among related regression problems. A common design treats effects as exchangeable across data groups while allowing correlations among covariates. This paper shows that this arrangement can perform poorly when covariates greatly outnumber groups, a situation that arises in high-dimensional applications such as statistical genetics.

The proposed alternative reverses the roles: effects are modeled as exchangeable across covariates, while correlations can differ across groups. Exchangeability specifies which effects receive a common probabilistic treatment. Changing that choice therefore changes how the model pools information. The authors construct a hierarchical model with this structure and an empirical Bayes estimator for learning correlations between groups.

Their theory demonstrates an advantage over the classic approach when the number of covariates dominates the number of groups. Experiments on several high-dimensional regression and classification problems support that result. The paper's message is tied to this dimensional regime: the direction in which a hierarchical model shares information can substantially affect statistical performance, and the conventional arrangement is not always the preferable one.
neurips-2021-for-high-dimensional-hierar.tldr: When covariates outnumber groups, exchanging their usual roles in a hierarchical model can improve statistical performance.

paragraphs: Different parameter settings in a stochastic model can produce identical observations, making inference ambiguous. A radio signal, for example, might come from a nearby weak source or a distant strong one. HNPE addresses this kind of indeterminacy by using additional observations that share some global parameters with the observation of interest.

The method places neural posterior estimation within a Bayesian hierarchical model. It extends simulation-based inference using normalizing flows so that information from the auxiliary observations can help constrain shared parameters. This changes the available evidence: relationships across observations can help distinguish explanations that are indistinguishable from a single observation alone.

The authors first validate the approach quantitatively on an example with an analytical solution. They then apply it to infer parameters of a nonlinear computational-neuroscience model using simulated and real EEG recordings. The contribution is a way to incorporate shared structure into neural inference. Its mechanism depends on the auxiliary observations conveying information through common global parameters, allowing the hierarchy to help resolve ambiguity in the underlying scientific model.
neurips-2021-hnpe-leveraging-global-para.tldr: HNPE uses observations with shared global parameters to help resolve ambiguity in simulation-based parameter inference.

paragraphs: Screen images are often reduced in resolution and compressed before transmission, then enlarged for viewing. Methods designed mainly for natural photographs do not generalize well to this setting, where image characteristics differ and users may zoom to arbitrary scales. This paper develops ITSRN specifically for continuous super-resolution of screen content.

The network predicts pixel values at requested coordinates using image features associated with key coordinates. This coordinate-based formulation supports arbitrary enlargement ratios. An implicit position-encoding scheme also combines similar neighboring pixel values when estimating a query pixel, contributing local information to the reconstruction.

The authors create SCI1K and SCI1K-compression benchmarks containing paired low- and high-resolution screen images. Experiments show significant improvements over several competitive methods that support either continuous or discrete scaling, for both compressed and uncompressed inputs. The contribution combines a reconstruction architecture suited to flexible zooming with evaluation data for screen-specific restoration. The findings support treating screen content and arbitrary output scale as central design requirements when building super-resolution methods for this use.
neurips-2021-implicit-transformer-networ.tldr: ITSRN reconstructs screen images at arbitrary enlargement ratios and improves results on compressed and uncompressed screen-content benchmarks.

paragraphs: Knowledge distillation transfers information from a teacher network to a student. Most approaches focus on training the student after the teacher is already available. This paper instead asks how to train a teacher whose learned representations will be easier for students to use.

During teacher optimization, the method jointly trains student branches to encourage representations that support knowledge transfer. The main intervention therefore happens while the teacher is being learned. The subsequent distillation procedure remains straightforward, allowing most existing distillation methods to adopt the technique and potentially improve student accuracy and convergence speed.

Experiments show strong accuracy across several established distillation techniques and different teacher–student combinations. The reported benefits also extend to cases where the architectures differ and the eventual student models are unknown during teacher training. This distinction matters: the jointly trained branches help shape the teacher, but the useful transfer is not restricted to a known final student architecture. The paper presents teacher preparation as a broadly compatible component of the distillation process.
neurips-2021-learning-student-friendly-t.tldr: Jointly training student branches with a teacher produces representations that improve later knowledge distillation.

paragraphs: Gaussian processes combined with deep networks can learn from few examples while representing uncertainty. This paper addresses how they can also reuse knowledge from related tasks. It proposes meta-learning a shared Gaussian-process prior through a collection of dense inducing variables.

Here, dense means that the inducing-variable set is much larger than the small support set available for each task. These variables collect information from previously experienced tasks and define a shared prior over prediction functions. They are learned using variational inference, giving new tasks a starting bias informed by related experience.

For a particular task, the method adapts the inducing variables with efficient gradient descent to obtain task-specific predictions. Experiments across common few-shot benchmarks report significant improvements over vanilla Gaussian processes and performance comparable to or better than state-of-the-art methods. The contribution joins shared knowledge and local adaptation within one probabilistic framework: the prior carries information across tasks, while adaptation lets a new task adjust that knowledge using its limited examples.
neurips-2021-learning-to-learn-dense-gau.tldr: Meta-learned dense inducing variables give Gaussian processes a reusable prior that improves few-shot learning.

paragraphs: Locating objects in three dimensions from a single image is difficult. Existing approaches may require heavy networks to combine image and depth information or struggle to use very large pseudo-LiDAR point sets effectively. The authors identify inaccurate object localization as a root cause of these limitations.

Their proposed Progressive Coordinate Transforms approach improves the learning of coordinate representations through successive localization refinement. A localization-boosting mechanism uses a confidence-aware loss to guide this process. The method also incorporates semantic image representations to compensate for its use of patch proposals, combining information about image content with coordinate-based localization.

Despite its lightweight design, the method achieves a new state-of-the-art result among monocular 3D detectors on the KITTI benchmark, according to the reported evaluation. The authors also report broad generalization to most coordinate-based detection frameworks. These findings support progressive localization refinement as a useful intervention for monocular detection. The approach emphasizes improving the quality of object-position estimates while remaining simple enough to fit into other coordinate-based detection systems.
neurips-2021-progressive-coordinate-tran.tldr: Progressive Coordinate Transforms refine object localization to improve lightweight monocular 3D detection.

paragraphs: Graph neural networks can struggle to connect information from distant parts of a graph. Simply making them deeper or wider can introduce optimization problems, including vanishing gradients and overly similar representations. GraphTrans addresses this by combining a standard graph neural network with a Transformer that learns long-range pairwise relationships.

The Transformer comes after the graph neural network and is permutation-invariant, so its operation does not depend on an arbitrary ordering of graph elements. A dedicated readout mechanism produces a representation of the whole graph. This arrangement lets the initial network process graph structure before global attention models broader relationships.

Experiments achieve state-of-the-art results on several graph-classification tasks, outperforming methods that explicitly encode graph structure in their long-range modeling. The results suggest that learned attention without additional graph-structure encoding can be suitable for high-level relationships. This is a qualified conclusion about the global modeling stage: GraphTrans still includes a standard graph neural network. Its contribution is an effective division of work between graph-based representation learning and global attention.
neurips-2021-representing-long-range-con.tldr: GraphTrans adds global Transformer attention after a graph neural network to improve graph classification through long-range relationships.

paragraphs: Policy-gradient methods learn by estimating how policy changes affect reward. With multiple agents, those estimates can become increasingly noisy as the number of agents grows. This paper analyzes that variance, separating the contributions of agent count and the agents' exploratory behavior.

Using the analysis, the authors derive a baseline that minimizes variance within the studied setting. A baseline is used in the gradient estimate to reduce noise. The paper measures the excess variance of existing methods, including vanilla multi-agent policy gradients and COMA, relative to this optimal baseline. It also proposes a surrogate version suitable for deep neural networks and integration into existing multi-agent policy-gradient methods.

Experiments on Multi-Agent MuJoCo and StarCraft challenges show more stable training and substantial performance improvements for multi-agent PPO and COMA. The contribution connects an analytical account of gradient noise with a practical intervention. The exact optimal baseline provides the theoretical reference, while the neural-network-oriented surrogate provides a way to use the idea in deep multi-agent learning.
neurips-2021-settling-the-variance-of-mu.tldr: An analysis of multi-agent gradient variance yields an optimal baseline and a practical surrogate that stabilize training in experiments.

paragraphs: A neural image denoiser implicitly contains information about which images are plausible. This paper develops a way to use that information for sampling and reconstruction tasks beyond denoising. It builds on a statistical connection between least-squares removal of additive Gaussian noise and the gradient of a noisy signal's log probability density.

From that connection, the authors derive a stochastic procedure that moves from coarse to fine scales to draw high-probability samples. The procedure uses a convolutional network trained for blind denoising. Extending it to constrained sampling allows the same implicit image prior to solve deterministic linear inverse problems without additional training.

The algorithm is described as relying on minimal assumptions and exhibiting robust convergence across a broad range of parameter choices. Demonstrations on deblurring, super-resolution, and compressive sensing reach state-of-the-art levels of unsupervised performance. These findings show how supervised denoising knowledge can support a wider class of reconstruction problems. The stated scope is deterministic linear inverse problems, and the reuse advantage comes from applying the already trained denoiser without task-specific retraining.
neurips-2021-stochastic-solutions-for-li.tldr: A stochastic sampler reuses a trained denoiser's implicit image prior to solve deterministic linear inverse problems without additional training.

paragraphs: Sequence-to-sequence models can struggle with new combinations of concepts that individually appeared during training. This paper addresses that systematic-generalization problem by explicitly modeling alignments between input and output segments. The alignments are discrete hidden structures learned within the neural model, avoiding the need to hand-engineer a grammar.

The proposed framework first reorders segments and then aligns them. Its neural reordering component produces separable permutations, giving structure to a potentially enormous search space. An efficient dynamic-programming algorithm computes exact marginal inference over these permutations, enabling end-to-end differentiable training despite the discrete reordering choices.

The resulting model generalizes more systematically than standard models on synthetic problems and on semantic parsing and machine translation tasks. The contribution links a structured account of how segments correspond with neural learning. Exact inference applies to the specified family of separable permutations, making the reordering component computationally manageable. The empirical findings support explicit latent alignment structure as a way to improve performance when test examples recombine familiar pieces in unfamiliar ways.
neurips-2021-structured-reordering-for-m.tldr: Learning structured segment reorderings and alignments improves systematic generalization in sequence-to-sequence models.

paragraphs: AdderNets replace multiplication-heavy convolutions with cheaper additions, offering energy-efficient networks with comparable performance. Their training, however, requires specialized adjustments, and their weights and activations can have very large variances. This paper studies those statistical properties as a route to making AdderNets more stable and useful.

The authors analyze variance estimates for the weights and output features of an arbitrary adder layer. Based on that analysis, they develop an adaptive weight-normalization scheme that adjusts the weight distribution during training. The scheme can reduce disturbances in the running mean and variance maintained by batch-normalization layers, addressing a concrete source of training instability.

The proposed normalization can also enhance adversarial robustness. Experiments across several benchmarks show higher-performing AdderNets using the approach. The contribution therefore connects layer-level variance analysis with practical training improvements and robustness benefits. It supports the idea that controlling weight distributions is consequential for addition-based networks, where unusually large weight and activation variances can otherwise restrict performance and the potential for broader use.
neurips-2021-towards-stable-and-robust-a.tldr: Adaptive weight normalization improves AdderNet training stability, performance, and adversarial robustness.

paragraphs: Video instance segmentation benefits from processing multiple frames together, but exchanging information across frames can require substantial computation and memory. This paper introduces Inter-frame Communication Transformers, an end-to-end approach designed to retain the benefits of clip-level context while reducing the cost of that communication.

The method uses compact memory tokens to summarize each frame and carry information between frames. Exchanging information through these tokens enriches frame features and connects them to other frames in the clip. The communication mechanism therefore operates through concise scene summaries, making temporal context less expensive to encode.

The authors report state-of-the-art performance on the evaluated benchmarks, including 42.6 average precision on the YouTube-VIS 2019 validation set with offline inference, alongside a reported runtime of 89.4 frames per second. The method also supports near-online inference, processing video in real time with a small delay. These results connect the architectural contribution to both segmentation quality and practical throughput, while distinguishing the reported offline accuracy result from the additional near-online operating mode.
neurips-2021-video-instance-segmentation.tldr: Compact memory tokens make communication between video frames more efficient while supporting strong instance-segmentation accuracy and fast inference.
